map.An Axiom City episode — Lessons 4-1 & 4-: An Axiom City episode — Lessons 4-1 & 4-2 at one time. It has three gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Market status: opens in ten minutes. Pie: The market opens in ten minutes. The pier has three cracks. The crew holds one hundred lanterns. With care.
map.Previously: on a rained-out field day, f: Last time: it rained on field day. Four sixth graders woke VEX in the old lab. VEX is a piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Then a fall storm broke the old pier. Tonight the Night Market opens to save it. Each stall, lantern and coin goes to fix it.
map.The waterfront, dusk. Stalls glowing, cr: The docks at dusk. The stalls glow. The crowd comes in. Hana and Eliot lug a big board up.
map.Easy — EASY! One hundred lanterns, ten r: Easy, EASY! One hundred lanterns, ten rows of ten. This board IS the fund drive, Eliot. Drop it and we lose the pier.
map.Relax, I've hauled rarer loot through wo: Relax. I have hauled loot through worse maps. It is a big progress bar. Each gift block lights one lantern.
map.Bram's Bargain Bay, by the gate! Deals s: Bram's Bargain Bay, by the gate! Deals so big they make no sense!
map.The board goes up over the square. An ho: The board goes up over the square. One hour in, the first gift blocks come.
map.Ms. Ortiz pledged the first blocks — twe: Ms. Ortiz gave the first blocks. Twenty-five lanterns are lit. Twenty-five out of one hundred.
The board does the math just by being there. 25 out of 100 is also the decimal 0.25. Same amount, new costume. But the PERCENT number is 25. No decimal point at all.
map.Definition loaded: a percent is a rate p: Here is the rule: a percent is a rate per hundred. 25 out of 100 = 25%. The sign % holds the "out of 100" for you. Write the count. Add the sign. Done.
map.A percent is a rate per hundred. On a hu: A percent is a rate per hundred. Use a hundred-grid. The shaded count out of 100 IS the percent. The decimal form (0.25) and the percent form (25%) match. They are the same amount. Just a new costume.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. T: Reader, you are our fifth crew member. The gifts are pouring in. The crowd wants numbers. Read the boards. Post the percents.
map.Hana's board holds 100 lanterns in a 10×: Hana's board has 100 lanterns in a 10×10 grid. Right now 60 are lit. Next to it, the raffle wall has 100 hooks. Just 7 of them hold a winning tag. The crowd needs both as percents.
map.Conceptual: percent means 'per hundred.': Conceptual: percent means 'per hundred.' Hana's board IS a hundred. So 'what percent is lit' has a simple meaning. It is how many of the hundred are lit. Same for the raffle wall.
map.Procedural: when the whole is exactly 10: Procedural: say the whole is just 100. Then the count out of 100 is the percent. Write the count. Put the % sign on it. Do not slide any decimal. A 0-point-something answer is the DECIMAL costume. The crowd wants the percent.
map.Every stall pledged a share of its sales: Each stall gave the pier a share of sales. But each stall wrote that share its own way. Fractions. Decimals. A mess.
map.The pier board only speaks percent. My t: The pier board only speaks percent. My tea stall's tag says 9/20. Divide top by bottom: 9 ÷ 20 = 0.45. Slide the decimal two places: 45%.
map.And the juice cart's 0.3? Slide twice: 3: And the juice cart's 0.3? Slide twice: 30%. Three forms, one truth.
map.Definition loaded: fraction → decimal →: Here is the rule: fraction → decimal → percent are three outfits for one amount. Divide top by bottom for the decimal. For the percent, make it per hundred: two decimal slides. The amount never changes. Only the costume.
map.To rewrite a fraction as a percent: divi: To write a fraction as a percent: divide the numerator by the denominator. Then move the decimal point two places right. Add the % sign. 9/20 = 0.45 = 45%.
map.Reader — the translator post is yours. T: Reader, you are the translator now. Two hard tags are left. Turn them into percent. Then the whole market reads one language.
map.Two stubborn tags. Tag A pledges 13/20 o: Two hard tags. Tag A gives 13/20 of each sale to the pier. Tag B gives 0.08 of each sale. The market board only speaks percent. Change them.
map.Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal and a: Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal and a percent: three costumes, ONE amount. The decimal is the bridge. Get it first. Then the percent is that amount, per hundred.
map.Procedural: Tag A — divide the top by th: Procedural: Tag A: divide top by bottom to get the decimal. Then slide the decimal point two places right. That gives the percent. Tag B is a decimal now. Read its HUNDREDTHS place, two slides right. Do not lose the zero after the point.
map.Tags translated, the crowd flows again —: The tags are done. The crowd moves again. It goes right past a stall. Its sign is still wet with paint.
map.Half off! HALF! You can't argue with hal: Half off! HALF! You can't argue with half, kids.
map.Half of WHAT, Bram? Your shelf tag still: Half of WHAT, Bram? Your shelf tag still says 0.2 of the "regular" price. Your sign and your tag do not agree.
map.Tonight's mission is lanterns, not lawsu: Tonight is for lanterns, not court fights. VEX, log the gate stall. We will come back with proof.
map.The pier itself, dark beyond the lantern: The pier, dark past the lanterns. The fix-up plan splits it into 25 planks. Gifts pay for them one by one.
map.Twenty-fifths don't speak percent yet —: Twenty-fifths do not speak percent yet. But 25 × 4 = 100. The snack stand paid for 6 planks. That was 6/25. Multiply top AND bottom by 4: 24/100. Twenty-four percent.
map.Scale the fraction to a hundred, then re: Scale the fraction to a hundred. Then read the percent right off. It is a free power-up.
map.When the denominator divides 100 evenly: Say the denominator divides 100 evenly (like 20, 25 or 50). Then scale the fraction to hundredths. Multiply top and bottom by the same number. The numerator is now the percent. 6/25 = 24/100 = 24%.
map.Closing time. The mayor's big board wait: Closing time. The mayor's board waits for the night's last news. Bram waits to argue with it.
map.My stall pledged point-four of sales. Or: My stall gave point-four of sales. Or 4%. Same thing, of course. Small dot, small change.
map.Reader — three locks. Ring the bell with: Reader, three locks. Ring the bell with TRUE numbers.
map.Boss Gate: turn the plank fraction into: Boss Gate: turn the plank fraction into a percent. Judge Bram's brag. Pick the honest poster grid.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. One bell. The pi: BOSS GATE. Three locks. One bell. The pier is listening. (No stress. Some stress.)
map.The mayor's board waits. Lock 1: the pie: The mayor's board waits. Lock 1: the pier banner says 19/25 planks are paid. Post it as a percent. Lock 2: Bram says a 0.4 pledge and a 4% pledge match. Which is larger? Lock 3: next week's poster must show 30%. Pick Hana's honest grid.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — a percent needs a p: Conceptual: Lock 1: a percent needs a per-hundred view. Twenty-fifths scale to hundredths because 25 × 4 = 100. Lock 2: a decimal and a percent are in two costumes. Never compare them as is. Change one first. Lock 3: is the grid's WHOLE just 100 parts? Only then does it show a percent. The shaded count alone proves nothing.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — multiply the banner: Procedural: Lock 1: multiply the banner fraction's top AND bottom by 4. Then read the numerator of the hundredths. Lock 2: slide the decimal's point two places right. See its percent. Then compare. Lock 3: in each grid, count shaded AND all squares. Then trust it.
…my stall still had the best lights.
map.And the dimmest math. See you next marke: And the worst math. See you next market night, Bram.
map.Six planks to go. And that gate stall's: Six planks to go. And the gate stall's "50% off"? It still does not say 50% off of WHAT.
map.New distortion at the gate stall: a perc: New glitch at the gate stall: a percent that hides its whole. To be continued…
map.Percent.\"Per hundred.\" A rate out of 1: Percent."Per hundred." A rate out of 100. In a hundred-grid, shaded count IS the percent. 60 lit lanterns out of 100 means 60%. And 7 out of 100 means 7%. No decimal point needed.
map.Fraction → decimal → percent.Three costu: Fraction → decimal → percent.Three costumes, one amount. Divide top by bottom for the decimal. Slide the decimal two places for the percent. 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%. The zero matters: 0.08 is 8%, not 80%.
map.Compare in one form.Never judge a decima: Compare in one form.A decimal and a percent in two costumes? Never judge them that way. 0.4 is 40%. That is ten times 4%. Does a grid's whole have just 100 parts? Only then is it a percent.
map.\"A hundred lanterns can hold any promis: "A hundred lanterns can hold any promise. Light them one per hundred." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 4 · Episode 1: Per Hundre: beat Unit 4 · Episode 1: Per Hundred. They know percents as rates per hundred. They link fraction–decimal–percent.
map.Thank you for lighting the board with th: Thank you for lighting the board with the crew. Episode 2 is being built now. Half off, whole missing.
map.Different board — the test string Hana w: A new board: Hana's test string at home. 45 of its 100 bulbs glow. Percent means per hundred. So 45 out of 100 is 45%. The count and the percent match. The whole is 100.
map.Costume check: 45 out of 100 is also the: Costume check: 45 out of 100 is also the decimal 0.45. Same amount, new clothes. The % sign holds the 'out of 100'. So the percent number stays 45, never 0.45.
map.Tiny counts work the same: 9 winning tic: Small counts work the same: 9 winning tickets out of 100 is 9%. Count, then %. That is the whole trick.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.A practice strip has 23 of its 100 bulbs: A test strip has 23 of its 100 bulbs lit. What percent of the strip is lit?
map.Different tag — the tea stall's 9/20. Di: A new tag: the tea stall's 9/20. Divide top by bottom: 9 ÷ 20 = 0.45. That is the decimal costume.
map.Decimal to percent: slide the point two: Decimal to percent: slide the point two places right. 0.45 turns into 45, so 9/20 = 45%. Same pledge, three outfits.
Watch the zero: the cocoa cart gave 0.06. Two slides right gives 6. Six HUNDREDTHS is 6%, never sixty. The zero between the point and the digit matters.
map.Translate the popcorn cart's 0.03 pledge: Turn the popcorn cart's 0.03 pledge into a percent.
map.Different banner — the snack count read: A new banner: the snack count was 7/25 sold. Scale to hundredths: 7 × 4 = 28 and 25 × 4 = 100, so 7/25 = 28/100 = 28%.
map.Costume duel with different numbers: com: Costume fight, new numbers: compare 0.6 with 6%. Slide 0.6 two places: 60%. The fight is over. Sixty per hundred beats six per hundred. The decimal was the bigger amount all along.
map.Grid check: 20 shaded squares mean 20% O: Grid check: 20 shaded squares mean 20% ONLY if the grid has 100 squares. In a 40-square grid, 20 shaded is 20/40. That is one half, or 50%. Count the whole first. Then trust the shading.
map.Scale the craft stall's 11/25 to a perce: Scale the craft stall's 11/25 to a percent.
map.Post something first — both boards need: Post something first. Both boards need a number.
That is the DECIMAL costume: six tenths. The % sign says 'per hundred' for you. So the percent is the lit count out of 100. No decimal slide needed.
map.Those are the DARK lanterns. The announc: Those are the DARK lanterns. The crowd wants to know what percent is LIT.
map.Look again — the board is exactly 100 la: Look again. The board is just 100 lanterns. Percent means per hundred. The lit count out of 100 IS the percent number.
map.That's the decimal — seven hundredths. T: That is the decimal: seven hundredths. The raffle wall wants the PERCENT: winners per hundred hooks.
map.Those are the empty hooks. The crowd wan: Those are the empty hooks. The crowd wants the WINNING tags.
map.The raffle wall holds exactly 100 hooks: The raffle wall has just 100 hooks. The winning count out of 100 is the percent.
map.Announcement posted! 60 of 100 lit is 60: Posted! 60 of 100 lit is 60%. And 7 winners out of 100 hooks is 7%. Percent means per hundred. The board said it all along.
map.Translate something first — three boxes: Fill in something first. Three boxes wait for numbers.
map.That's the PERCENT costume in the decima: That is the PERCENT costume in the decimal box. This tag's decimal is between 0 and 1. Divide the top by the bottom.
map.Tag A's decimal: divide 13 by 20 — top b: Tag A's decimal: divide 13 by 20, top by bottom. Keep what the division gives you.
map.That's the decimal again — it already li: That is the decimal again. It is in the first box now. Slide it two places right to get percent.
map.Decimal locked. Now slide its point two: Decimal done. Now slide its point two places right. Add the % sign.
map.The zero matters — 0.08 is eight HUNDRED: The zero matters. 0.08 is eight HUNDREDTHS, not eight tenths. Eighty per hundred would be 0.80. That is a much bigger pledge.
map.That's the decimal it already wears. Per: That is the decimal it has now. Make it per hundred: slide the point two places right.
map.Tag B: read the hundredths. Two slides r: Tag B: read the hundredths. Two slides right. Watch the zero between the point and the 8.
map.Translated! 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%, and 0.08: Done! 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%, and 0.08 = 8/100 = 8%. Three costumes, one amount. Now the market speaks one language.
map.Lock 1 first — the banner number leads t: Lock 1 first. The banner number comes first on the board.
map.Lock 1 holds. 19 is only the TOP of the: Lock 1 is shut. 19 is just the TOP of the fraction. It is out of 25, not out of 100. Scale the whole fraction to hundredths.
map.Lock 1 holds. That's the decimal costume: Lock 1 is shut. That is the decimal costume. The big board speaks percent: per hundred.
map.Lock 1 holds. 25 × 4 = 100 — multiply BO: Lock 1 is shut. 25 × 4 = 100. Multiply BOTH parts of 19/25 by 4. Then read the hundredths.
map.Lock 1 open! Lock 2: put both pledges in: Lock 1 open! Lock 2: put both pledges in the SAME costume. Then judge them.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4 looks bigger than 0.4 —: Lock 2 is shut. 4 looks bigger than 0.4. But slide 0.4 two places: it is 40 per hundred. Forty percent against four.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's Bram's exact claim: Lock 2 is shut. That is just what Bram said. The bell says no. Slide 0.4 two places right. It is not 4 per hundred.
map.Locks 1 and 2 open! Lock 3: count shaded: Locks 1 and 2 open! Lock 3: count shaded AND all squares in each grid. A percent grid must show its amount per HUNDRED.
map.Lock 3 holds. That grid lights 3 of 100: Lock 3 is shut. That grid lights 3 of 100. That is 3%. Ten times too small for the poster.
map.Lock 3 holds. Thirty squares glow, but t: Lock 3 is shut. Thirty squares glow. But that grid only HAS fifty. 30 out of 50 is 60%. Percent needs a hundred parts in the whole.
map.Lock 3 holds. 13 of 100 is 13% — not eve: Lock 3 is shut. 13 of 100 is 13%. Not even half of the goal poster.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 19/25 = 76/100 — the bel: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 19/25 = 76/100. The bell rings: 76% paid. 0.4 is 40%, ten times Bram's 4%. Only the 30-of-100 grid truly says 30%. The market ends loud. The pier fund glows.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
